subject: North-source public park and elevated roof / public-realm edges

coordinate_convention.polygon_order: clockwise as viewed in the source image unless noted
coordinate_convention.line_order: ordered along the visible feature; endpoints are not world-space anchors
coordinate_convention.trace_precision_px: approximately ±10–25 px depending on crowd, trees, lighting and perspective occlusion

high_resolution_cross_check.relationship: same north/B4 proposal view; use the original source above for the coordinates in this file

source.inspection_note: The park edge is clearest between the stadium entry plaza, the large east hall, the lower riverfront retail edge and the road-side corner. The far east roof garden is not part of these public-park traces.

integration_guidance.use: Inverse-project the roof/deck traces through the calibrated north camera only at a candidate intermediate public-realm plane, then validate against a fresh detail-north render. Keep the Roosevelt road/sidewalk and the covered rail links as separate datum hypotheses until a camera-fit and connectivity check resolves their relationship.
do_not: Do not use the vertices as surveyed world coordinates.
Do not fill the roof polygon as one blank lawn; preserve the four lawn rooms and hard paved/path separators.
Do not force hidden facade or stair geometry where the source is occluded.
integration_guidance.primary_correction: The source reads as a compact irregular roof/deck with connected lawn rooms and deliberate paths. The current v3 outline is too large and rectangular; shrink to the traced envelope first, then add paths, stairs and planting within it.

trace_status: Supersedes revision 2 for elevation interpretation. The source-edge traces are unchanged; the public road/sidewalk is separated from the private covered rail links, and no upper public plaza is assigned the implementation z=22 datum.

source_read.relation: below the park roof; the source exposes a continuous lower facade and active walk beneath the upper lawn edge
a raised public deck between the lower retail level and the hall/stadium-facing entries; the image establishes ordering, not a surveyed absolute height

The quoted entry is interpreted as the Roosevelt road/viaduct sidewalk approaching directly above the outfield bleachers. The source supports a public entry relationship and an above-bleacher visual ordering, but does not resolve an independent pedestrian viaduct or an absolute upper world elevation.

source_read.feature: Roosevelt vehicle road and sidewalk versus covered rail links
source_read.relation: Roosevelt road and its sidewalk are the public transport/entry edge in this interpretation. The covered rail crossings are separate private east-west links over the tracks; they must not define the public plaza datum. Their world-level relationship to the park roof is unresolved in the aerial.

constrained_relations: park_lawn_or_roof_deck_z should connect to the hall/stadium public realm through a visible short transition; the source does not justify assigning it the vehicle-road datum by itself
the Roosevelt road/sidewalk edge is a candidate public entry datum above or alongside the outfield edge; exact grade, ramp and stair geometry remain unresolved
covered pedestrian rail-link decks are private crossings and do not establish the public Roosevelt plaza datum
a plaza described as entering directly above the bleachers must be modeled as a separate upper landing/entrance relationship, not by lifting every lawn polygon

interpretation_for_integration.lower_level: Keep the lower waterside walk as the lower public level candidate; its absolute z remains inferred.
interpretation_for_integration.park_level: Treat the compact lawn roof as an intermediate public deck. Current z=8.65 is an implementation prior only; it must not be reused for a Roosevelt road-level plaza without a camera-fit and continuity check.
interpretation_for_integration.upper_entry: Do not use covered-crossing z=22 as a public upper-entry datum. The source-backed candidate is the Roosevelt road plus sidewalk at the east edge, but its world z and its connection to the outfield entrance are unresolved. Keep any separate upper landing as explicitly inferred.
interpretation_for_integration.vehicle_viaduct: Keep road/bridge deck z=14.1–14.25 as the existing implementation prior for Roosevelt transport geometry. Test a public grade transition to the park/stadium entry only where the source edge aligns; do not connect it automatically to the private rail-crossing deck.

datum_provenance.source_support: The source establishes visible ordering, adjacency and access relationships. It does not provide survey elevations or enough orthographic control to recover world z values.
datum_provenance.covered_pedestrian_crossing_deck_z: private rail-link integration prior only; not evidence for a Roosevelt public plaza
datum_provenance.roosevelt_vehicle_road_z: existing road/bridge implementation prior; public-edge candidate, not source-measured

source_grade_correspondences.coordinate_basis: Approximate image-plane paths in the canonical original north source; points locate visible edges and do not encode world elevation.

mapping_from_canonical.method: derived resize correspondence; use for inspection only

features.name: roosevelt_road_carriageway_band
features.evidence: Visible multi-lane roadway along the far east image edge; perspective, crop and lighting make the inner/outer curb edges approximate.
features.grade_claim: Locates the public road corridor only; no absolute or shared z is implied.

features.name: roosevelt_sidewalk_inner_edge
features.evidence: Bright pedestrian strip between the east hall/park edge and the road; trees, crowds and the image boundary occlude several junctions.
features.grade_claim: Candidate public entry edge for connectivity tests; its world elevation remains unresolved.

features.name: east_park_to_road_public_edge
features.evidence: Approximate path/plaza continuation from the southeast lawn and crowd gathering toward the east sidewalk; exact tie-in is hidden by people and planting.
features.grade_claim: Supports testing a public continuity relationship only; it does not prove a ramp, stair or level match.

features.name: park_roof_east_edge
features.evidence: Existing traced roof/deck boundary around the east lawn rooms, with the lower retail edge excluded.
features.grade_claim: Confirms the park boundary in image space; no relationship to Roosevelt road z is proven.

features.name: covered_private_rail_links
features.evidence: Covered east-west links visibly cross the tracks behind the hall; they are distinct enclosed/private circulation pieces.
features.grade_claim: Do not use these links as evidence for the public Roosevelt plaza elevation.

source_grade_correspondences.interpretation_boundary: These correspondences are for tracing and camera-fit tests. They establish candidate edge continuity and feature separation, not a surveyed grade profile.
